rationale:
Evidence: iteration 7 tested kd 0.25 alone against the iteration 6 baseline (kp 2.0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1). It scored 163.3, down from 354.2. Oval completion fell from 16/20 to 1/20, oval line_loss_events rose from 0.85 to 1.3, and oval max_error rose from 0.048 to 0.063, reaching the 0.06 off-track limit. Oval steering_oscillation also rose, from 0.327 to 0.365, so the hypothesis that lower kd would reduce jitter is contradicted. Lower kd gave less damping on the bends, which is the risk the Evaluator flagged. Following the Evaluator's rule, I revert kd to 0.3. The narrow five-sensor geometry, sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], ki 0 and last_direction stay unchanged, and kp stays at 2.0, the value that improved line retention in iteration 6.

Change: base_speed 1.1 to 1.2, as the single variable. This restores the best raced controller (iteration 6) and adds one speed step. Speed 1.1 is the only tested setting between 0.9 (worse, iteration 5) and 1.3 (worse at kp 2.5 and kd 0.3, iteration 1), and 1.2 has not been tested. Oval mean finish time was about 1.96 s at 1.1, so there is time margin under 3.0 s. The aim is to lift oval and s-bend progress and completion time while keeping line loss at or below iteration 6 levels.

Expected result: oval completion holds near 80% with line_loss_events at or below 0.85 and max_error at or below 0.048. Oval completion_time may fall slightly. The s-bend and slalom still have line loss near 1 per run, so they may stay off track. Risk: higher speed could raise line loss on the tight bends. If line_loss_events or max_error rise, the next step is to return to base_speed 1.1 and test a small kp change (about 1.8) alone, since iteration 6 showed kp reduction helped line retention.

Hypotheses to test: (a) the kp 2.0 and kd 0.3 controller is near a local optimum, and a modest speed increase will shorten run time without raising line loss; (b) the s-bend and slalom failures come from line loss on the bends, not from sensor coverage.

Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, plus noise_robustness.
